question: In a woman with early breast cancer and a clinically node-negative axilla, sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is the standard procedure to stage the axilla and avoids the morbidity of routine axillary lymph node dissection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Sentinel lymph node biopsy has replaced routine axillary lymph node dissection for staging in node-negative early breast cancer, because a negative SLNB predicts the rest of the axilla to be clear — with far less morbidity than complete axillary dissection.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SLNB is now the standard of care for axillary staging in clinically node-negative early breast cancer. It samples only the sentinel node(s) (the first draining nodes), and if negative, spares the patient a full axillary clearance — significantly reducing lymphoedema risk.
